blocks.text: The Name Al-Muqeet The All-Powerful Maintainer appears once in the Qur'aan,

Whosoever intercedes for a good cause will have the reward thereof, and whosoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a share in its burden. And Allah is Ever All-Able to do (and also an All-Witness to) everything.
Ibn Katheer said about: 'And Allah is Ever All-Able to do (and also an All-Witness to) everything.'
Ibn 'Abbaas, 'Ataa, 'Atiyyah, Qataadah and Matar al-Warraaq said, 'Muqeeta' means 'Protector'.
Mujaahid said 'Witness' and in another narration by him he said 'Taker to account'.
Sa'eed bin Jubayr, Suddee and Ibn Zayd said 'All-Able'.
'Abdullaah bin Katheer said Al-Muqeet means 'The Lasting'.
Ad-Dahhaak said Al-Muqeet is Ar-Razzaaq 'The Provider'.

Nothing prevents this Name from encompassing all of these meanings so that it carries the meaning: The One whose knowledge encompasses the servants, their situations and what they need. He encompasses them with power as He is able to do all things, He protects, provides and helps them. The One who sustains the bodies with food and provision; and sustains the hearts of whomever He wishes of His servants with knowledge and faith.

keyPoints: Al-Muqeet appears once in the Qur'aan, in Nisaa 4:85.

Ibn Katheer reported the explanations of the Salaf: 'Protector' (Ibn 'Abbaas and others), 'Witness' or 'Taker to account' (Mujaahid), 'All-Able' (Sa'eed bin Jubayr and others), 'The Lasting' ('Abdullaah bin Katheer), and 'The Provider' (Ad-Dahhaak).
Nothing prevents this Name from encompassing all of these meanings.
Al-Muqeet is the One whose knowledge encompasses the servants, their situations and needs, and who is able to do all things, protecting, providing for and helping them.
He sustains the bodies with food and provision, and sustains the hearts of whomever He wishes with knowledge and faith.

evidence.text: And Allah is Ever All-Able to do (and also an All-Witness to) everything.

recall.q: What does Al-Muqeet mean, combining the meanings mentioned?
recall.a: The One whose knowledge encompasses the servants, their situations and what they need; He encompasses them with power, protects, provides and helps them; He sustains the bodies with food and provision and the hearts of whomever He wishes with knowledge and faith.

recall.q: How many times does Al-Muqeet appear in the Qur'aan, and where?
What did Ibn 'Abbaas, 'Ataa, 'Atiyyah, Qataadah and Matar al-Warraaq say 'Muqeeta' means?

recall.a: He said Al-Muqeet is Ar-Razzaaq, 'The Provider'.

recall.q: What did Mujaahid say Al-Muqeet means?
recall.a: 'Witness', and in another narration 'Taker to account'.
